topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and sets out the learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens.

topics.label: Conceptual frameworks and epidemiological evidence for cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises through genetic and microenvironmental changes and review the epidemiological evidence and debates regarding intrinsic versus environmental risk factors.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the discovery and mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental, dietary, and occupational mutagens inflict DNA damage through direct alterations, xenobiotic metabolic activation, and bulky adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic contributors to cancer, including chronic inflammation, initiator-promoter dynamics, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic signature profiling, epidemiological studies, animal models, and in vitro tests used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Summary of cancer risk-benefit decisions and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by discussing risk-benefit trade-offs with environmental exposures and delivering final closing remarks.
